Build Shorts around a named, real case people already know, not a generic 'what if this happens to you'. Sahara, Vodafone Idea and 2G/coal kept 36%, 28% and 24% of viewers to the end. Wedding shagun and wrong UPI kept 14% and 12%.

At scenes 3-4 (the 25-50% mark), bring in a new number or a new stake for the viewer instead of explaining the logic. Sahara and Vodafone lost under 20% of their remaining viewers there, and Vodafone's second scene added a bigger figure plus 'iska bill aap tak
Deliver the answer by the 75% mark and end within one line of it. UPI fell from 41 to 14 viewers and shagun from 31 to 16 in the last quarter, while Sahara only slipped from 79 to 62.

Long videos: open with a two-number contradiction that matches the title, and delete warm-up lines like 'Chaliye, shuru se dekhte hain' and 'Aaiye, sach jaante hain'. The ghar video ('50 lakh ka ghar, bill 1 crore') still had 44% at the 5% mark. Naukri still h

Long videos: do not spend the first 30-60 seconds on family backstory ('Amit aur Neha ki kahani suniye. Dono naukri karte hain...'). Start the story at the money moment. Both 11-minute videos had only 20-27% of viewers left by the 10% mark (about one minute in

sglearning.report:
Shorts are working: the five with enough views kept 80-95% of viewers past the first tenth. Sahara was best, with 92% watched on average and 36% staying to the very end.
Long videos are the problem: both 11-minute videos lost over half their viewers in the first 30 seconds, and only 3-6% reached the end. The car video (38 views) is too small to judge.
Shorts about famous real cases (Sahara, Vodafone Idea, 2G/coal) kept 24-36% to the end; everyday 'what if' Shorts (wedding gift, wrong UPI) kept only 12-14%.
The last four English Shorts opened with a slow setup sentence, and 68-76% swiped away on Instagram within 3 seconds, versus 59% for Shorts that opened straight on the question. They show 0 YouTube views, so please check they were actually published there. The insurance Short had only 5 Instagram views, too few to judge.
The 'open on picture vs open on presenter' test cannot be judged

lessons: Open with one question of about 10 words that names the character and the strange fact, such as 'Prayagraj ke Hanuman ji khade nahi, lete hue kyun hain?' or 'Boodhe Jatayu ne Ravan ka rath sach mein toda tha?'. These two had the fewest Instagram swipes in the

Open on the drama (a fight, a trick, a curse), not on a custom. Tulsi opened with 'why is the wedding done with a stone' and held the trick and the curse until scenes 2 and 3. 65.1% swiped away in 3 seconds on Instagram, 14 points worse than any other Short.

Make the title, the spoken hook and the first on-screen line ask the same question, and never start mid-story with an unnamed person. In Hanuman janm, Padmini, Hayagriva and Bharat, the spoken hook differed from the first line, and all four lost 45.6% to 50.4%

Do not admit 'the texts don't say' before the halfway point; keep a new clue in every scene. Hanuman janm says 'katha pahad ka pata nahi deti' in scene 3. Between the 10% and 25% marks it fell from 94 to 61, the steepest drop of any Short with 50 or more views

Give the answer before the 75% mark and end within about 5 seconds of it, with no recap or outro. In every Short we could measure, more than half of the remaining viewers left in the last quarter: Vishnu 51 to 20, Jatayu 49 to 23, Hanuman lete 41 to 15, Hanuma

In long videos, put the hard evidence on screen within the first 40 seconds (the 1985 Panchganga record, the Chausath inscription). Cut filler like 'Aaiye isko samajhte hain', and don't say 'bina kagzi sabut' up front. Both long videos lost 56 of every 100 vie

arthvan.report:
Shorts keep viewers well: 85 to 100 of every 100 are still watching at the 10% mark. Our two long videos keep only 26.
Long videos lose 56 of every 100 viewers in the first 45 seconds, which is our biggest leak.
Best: Jatayu (1,080 Instagram views, only 43.5% swiped away early). Weakest opening: Tulsi (65% swiped away in 3 seconds).
Ignore for now: Manthara's numbers are broken (341% watched). Tulsi, Kirtimukha and Padmini had under 50 YouTube views. Padmini's 79-second Instagram watch time looks wrong.
Check: three videos from 26–27 Nov show 0 YouTube views. No video was tagged for the picture-vs-presenter test, so that test has no result yet.
The one change: start every video with one short question (about 10 words) naming the character and the strange fact, worded the same as the title.
